Why did the old way not work? I wonder if it broke at some point and we just failed to notice.

In principle, deferring this to morph (or retrying this during morph) may catch a few more cases (say somebody wraps one of these in a helper, for some reason).

> Why did the old way not work? I wonder if it broke at some point and we just failed to notice.
> 
> In principle, deferring this to morph (or retrying this during morph) may catch a few more cases (say somebody wraps one of these in a helper, for some reason).

I think it's https://github.com/dotnet/coreclr/pull/21328, it introduced a field to cache Thread.CurrentThread - so `get_CurrentThread` is inlined as `s_currentThread ?? InitaliseCurrentThread()` (used to be an internalcall). 

Perhaps, it makes sense to add a benchmark next to this: https://github.com/dotnet/performance/blob/master/src/benchmarks/micro/libraries/System.Threading/Perf.Thread.cs#L13-L14

so the fact that `get_CurrentThread` is inlined into a field check + init makes it harder to handle in morph I guess.

Re: dropping the call to initialize the field. 

Since we have intrisified this it's ok to disregard certain side effects if the result is unused and the call is known to be idempotent and exception free. Since you're in the importer you can be sure there is no other user of the call's result (otherwise it would have been spilled to a temp). 

To try and also catch this in morph you might perhaps try something like what I did for the similar EqualityComparer case (look for `GTF_CALL_M_HELPER_SPECIAL_DCE`). Not sure it's worth the trouble though.

> I think it's dotnet/coreclr#21328, it introduced a field to cache Thread.CurrentThread - so get_CurrentThread is inlined as s_currentThread ?? InitaliseCurrentThread() (used to be an internalcall).

Could that be made faster as a helper for the many variants of InlineGetThread asm?

> > I think it's [dotnet/coreclr#21328](https://github.com/dotnet/coreclr/pull/21328), it introduced a field to cache Thread.CurrentThread - so get_CurrentThread is inlined as s_currentThread ?? InitaliseCurrentThread() (used to be an internalcall).
> 
> Could that be made faster as a helper for the many variants of InlineGetThread asm?

not sure I understand what you mean 🙂

bonus change: make `CORINFO_HELP_GETCURRENTMANAGEDTHREADID` pure.
e.g.:
```csharp

{
    int id = Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId; // unused
}
```


> Benchmark:
> [Benchmark]
> public int CurrentThreadId() => Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId;

The performance of `Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId` should be fixed by converting it to FCall that just does the right thing. It does not make sense to depend on JIT optimizations to do this. It is how it was done in .NET Framework, but it was deoptimized in early .NET Core days when Environment did not live in CoreLib.

> > Benchmark:
> > [Benchmark]
> > public int CurrentThreadId() => Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId;
> 
> The performance of `Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId` should be fixed by converting it to FCall that just does the right thing. It does not make sense to depend on JIT optimizations to do this. It is how it was done in .NET Framework, but it was deoptimized in early .NET Core days when Environment did not live in CoreLib.

What about `Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId`?

e.g. aspnetcore repo:
`Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId` usages: 6
`Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId` usages: 0

I honestly never used `Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId` API. But your suggestion makes things a lot easier I agree.

> What about Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId?

Yes, this optimization is still useful to fix `Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId`. It may be also worth having analyzer that suggests converting `Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId` to `Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId`.
@EgorBo Are you still working on this?

@BruceForstall I think it's finished - it does optimize `Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId` call sequence.

we don't need this optimization if we rewrite all `Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId` usages to `Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId` but looks like developers tend to prefer the former one.

I have opened https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/43257 on adding the analyzer. I think having analyzer for this is a good idea independ on whether we keep this as a pattern match optimization in the JIT.

So if we're fine with the analyzer (I filed a PR against aspnetcore to replace `Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId` with `Env.CurrentManagedThreadId` https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/27244) I can just remove traces of the optimization in JIT or we can merge it as is (it works).

I think we should probably handle this in the jit as there are likely many uses of  `Thread...` out there that might never get changed.

Can you resolve the conflicts?

issue_context.body:

but I don't see it happening in the following code:
```csharp
static int CurrId() => Thread.CurrentThread.ManagedThreadId;
```
